source: Clemence just wants you to be okay.
Clemence thinks, respectfully, that you're an angry kid.
You made Clemence believe things can change.
You convinced Clemence you're right.
Clemence seems happy. Well done.
You made Clemence consider that something needs to change.
You gave Clemence something to think about.
You told Clemence you would speak up to your father.
You swore to kill your father.
You told Clemence you were planning on starting something new.
Clemence appreciates that.
You asked Clemence to lie.
Clemence thinks your concern is unfounded.
Clemence is thinking about what you said.
Carlo doesn't know Clemence took you along.
Carlo allowed Clemence to take you along.
Clemence doesn't believe change is possible.
...Stay by the car.
Why? Why are you acting like this?
Don't tell me what to do. We're in this together now.
You need my help, uncle. Face it.
...Well, sometimes deals go sour. Or someone needs taking care of. There are rules, and when those rules are broken, well...they need to be enforced.
Speak plainly.
And that's "cleanup"?
So it's killing.
It wasn't like this. There was a sense of honour to what we did. A sense of tradition, of respect. Now it's...profit.
Now it's my father running things. That's the real issue.
Grandpa wouldn't be very happy about it.
It doesn't have to be like this, you know. Things could change.
So do I, Clarissa. A lot has has changed. Some for the worse, some for the better.
And among the "worse", my father.
Mostly for the worse, it seems.
It doesn't have to be like that. Not all change is for the better.
...Come on. Let's get up on the dam - if nothing else, the view is nice. It'll cheer us right up.
[Keep walking]
...What do you mean?
(AMBITIOUS) This all started with my father's leadership. A rotten kingdom is only as rotten as its ruler. Maybe there's hope in the line of succession.
(CUNNING) Things are the way they are because it's easy. No one's put any thought in it - no one that matters, anyway. Not yet.
(POWERFUL) I'm saying nothing's eternal - change just comes about when you bring it to the table. I can do that.
I know you have your differences, kid. We...you may not agree with everything he does, but he does what he can. Now come on, let's get up these stairs. The view's nice.
[Keep walking]
You think...you'd do things differently?
I'm sure as shit not as rotten as him.
I don't know. I'd just try to be more like grandpa than my father.
You and me both, uncle. People who care about the old days.
...And you'd be the one to bring about that change? Am I hearing that correctly?
All I know is that anything is better than what my father is doing.
I just want things to be done the way grandpa did them.
Not just me, uncle. You as well. And everyone else who cares about the old ways.
...Clarissa, your father is a powerful man. You don't just tell powerful men what to do.
He's a coward in big, ill-fitting shoes. Nothing powerful about him.
Why the fuck not?
No. All you need to do is to be better than them. Do it like they did back in the day.
That...does sound nice. But before you go on changing the world, kid, how about we get up to the top of this dam? The view's real nice. Come on.
[Keep walking]
...She was just a kid. We don't do that, we don't just dump...kids. That's not who we are.
It is now, apparently.
Not you and me, no. But my father. Some of our people, perhaps.
You're right. It's not. But some seem to have forgotten that.

So - we usually refer to these things as...well, cleanup. Or a sweep. 'Course, back in the day, we called it a "touch-up". Changing terms is good, though. Little confusing for old heads like mine, but you make do.
So the terminology changed, but the work remained the same?
You seem to be doing fine, old man.
So what is a cleanup, exactly?
Perspective. I suppose that's one of the few good things about coming here, eh? Can't get much further out than this.
I wish I could.
Doesn't make it any less depressing, nor more beautiful.
[Look at the view] You're right. It is nice.
Almost there. Might as well enjoy a moment of respite until then. This place, it ain't pretty - the view helps you remember that it isn't all this bad.
Sometimes I wish I could escape - not just this place, but the City. Everything.
I'm not so sure, uncle. The City doesn't look much more appealing from here.
[Look at the view] Maybe not, after all.
It's there, make no mistake. You just need to look for it. See past the clouds, past the grey.
Nevermind seeing - I'd like to go there. Far out, beyond the wall.
The City looks the same. Gray, foggy. Dark.
[Look out at the City] I suppose it is out there, somewhere. I guess that's comforting.
Hah. Well, even if you did, there isn't much out there. Wastes, I'm told - far as the eye can see. Nothing.
You're not curious?
There goes that dream, I suppose.
Not at all. Plenty of trouble inside the Wall as it is. Plenty of beauty, too. You just need to learn to see it.
That sounds like a distraction from reality, more than anything else.
Maybe. You might be right, uncle.
Don't take it too hard, Clarissa. Plenty of discoveries to be made inside the Wall, too. Just need to look for it.
That's not enough - a distraction, at best.
Yeah. You might be right about that.
But that doesn't make your home any less real, does it? Doesn't make a warm meal or a soft bed any less comforting.
Nor does it make the prospect of leaving the City any less interesting.
Be happy for the smaller things. That's what you're saying?
That's what keeps you going - that's what I've found, at least.
Maybe. Or maybe it's just a convenient distraction.
I'm not so sure. I'd rather look forward, at what could be.
You might be right about that, uncle.
Good. We'd lose our minds if all we did was imagine what things could be, instead of seeing them for what they are.
I'd rather see them for what they could be.
So enjoy the little things? That's your wisdom?
Hah. Just remember, Clarissa - dreams easily shift into fantasy, and fantasy never got anyone anywhere.
(AMBITIOUS) You're wrong. Ambition gets us anywhere.
(CUNNING) Neither does letting your guard down. There's always something to consider, something to plan for.
(POWERFUL) Nobody ever got anything without claiming it, either.
...Yeah. Maybe so.
...Told you, didn't I? You can see real far from here.
The City seems so distant. So miniscule.
I'm more concerned about the body we're here for.
I'll take your word for it. All I see is fog and concrete.
I think I am. I'm glad you see it the same way, Clarissa. Maybe you coming out here wasn't so bad, after all.
...There's still a body we need to tend to.
Told you, didn't I?
Then what's got you so distracted, kid? It's got to be something big, if everything else pales in comparison.
(AMBITIOUS) Ambition, I suppose.
(CUNNING) Everything. There's always something to consider, something to plan for.
(POWERFUL) The family. Its future. What I do next.
...Nothing. Maybe this is the distraction I need. Maybe you are right.
Quite right. Come on, then. Not much further, if my instinct proves correct.
[Keep walking]
Let's take our time. I'd like to enjoy this moment, if only a little longer.
That I can get behind. You're a good kid, Clarissa. You remind me of your grandfather.
...You remind me of him.
[Take your time]
...Alright, I'm getting tired. Let's get a move on.
Come on. Let's pick up the pace.
..."Come end of fall, the winds will grow, then twisting branches cusp the snow..."
...Not much further now. Almost there.
[Keep walking]
"...But spring will free what cold held dear; give way, give way, for one more year." I know that one. It's a nice poem.
Yeah. It is. [Keep walking]
Grandpa taught it to me. I can't believe I still remember it.
That's always the case with the things that matter most. You don't forget, even if you tried.
[Keep walking]
You're right. You don't.
Mhm. Me and the other capos use this place for all sorts of things - deals, arguments, meetings...and disposal.
Meetings?
Deals?
Arguments?
Disposal?
Hah. Good. Good, good.
...Are we there yet?
[Keep walking]
Ambitions are fickle things, kid. Same as dreams, same as fantasy.
Only if you lack the conviction to realize them.
Don't you have any ambition, uncle?
Fine - then all I dream of now is to get across this dam.
That may be - but you spend your whole life thinking of tomorrow, and today will never matter.
Today already matters little. Not the way it is, anyway.
Don't you ever think about tomorrow? What you want, the things you aspire to?
Then let's get today over with. How much further?
And what about now? What about what you want, in this moment? Not in a day, or a week, or a year - but now?
Not this - that's all I know. This isn't enough.
You don't understand, uncle. Don't you have any dreams? Aspirations for tomorrow?
...Fine. Getting across this dam would be a good start.
I...it shouldn't have gone like this. You shouldn't have seen that. I told you that it wasn't going to be pretty. I shouldn't have brought you here.
No, you should have. This is the catalyst. This is what will wake you up.
Maybe not. But you did, and now we live with it. We move forward.
Who cares what I see or don't see? What happened to that girl - that's what matters.
I know you want...change, Clarissa. But you can't force that. If you do, you end up changing nothing.
Doesn't mean I won't try.
So the lesson is to never try? Not very inspiring, uncle.
That's easy for you to say, uncle. Not everyone's lot in life is as agreeable as yours.
I've learned to settle, to be happy with my lot. It makes life a lot easier, a lot more enjoyable.
I can't settle, uncle. I won't.
So you're content to wallow in mediocrity? I see.
That's easy for you to say, uncle. Not everyone's lot is as agreeable as yours.
Not to worry - we're almost there.
[Keep walking]
I see that. Come on - we're almost there. Just down these stairs, now.
[Keep walking]
...We're almost there. Keep your chin up, Clarissa. Just down these stairs, now.
[Keep walking]
Clarissa. Stay. By. The. Car.
No. This is exactly what I mean. It doesn't have to be like this.
What will it take, uncle? You know I'm right!
Wake up, Clemence! These aren't the good old days anymore!
...Fine. If you can't stomach me being part of this, fine.
No, I...I suppose not. Hm. Ah - look. We're almost there. Just down these stairs, and we've arrived.
[Keep walking]
She's...I...Shepherd save us.
...Shit. Let's get to work.
This is what our people do? The people we're supposed to trust?!
...What happened here?
This is...that's a body. Dead. She's dead.
Just...look away. We'll head back to the car.
...Not yet.
This is what our people do? The people we're supposed to trust?!
Wait - we need to find out what happened, don't we?
This is...that's a body. Dead. She's dead.
...Just a...kid...just a little girl.
...Shit. Let's get to work.
...This is what our people do? The people we're supposed to trust?!
...What happened here?
Dead.
I'm going to get to work on bringing about real change. Just you watch.
Things can be different, uncle. But for that to happen, I need you by my side.
This family has rotted from the inside ever since my father took charge. That needs to change.
...What is your plan, exactly?
I'm going to confront my father. I'm done staying silent.
This family, this organization - it's done for. It's time to start something new. A syndicate.
I'm going to kill the bastard.
...Good. It might be long over due. Do you think he'll listen?
I'll make him listen.
Not without your help.
...Clarissa, take a deep breath. Compose yourself. You're not...you wouldn't kill your own father, would you?
Not under ordinary circumstances, no. He forced my hand.
I would. Gladly.
What other choice is there? He is the source of all this...rot.
...You're thinking of leaving the family? Your name?
Yes. And I need your help.
The name means nothing anymore. That much is clear.
I'm...I'll think on it. I've always been a Bloodworth. Never thought that would change - could change.
You won't have to. I just need your help to find a way out.
Just think about it. That's all I ask.
...We're going back to the car. Now.
Uncle, listen to me.
...Yeah. Alright.
What - NOW you don't have the stomach for it?!
That...that I could do. Perhaps. I'll need to think about it. For now, there's still...the body. I need to take care of it.
Don't worry. I'll stay here.
I'm coming with you.
Let's...talk about it. No brash decisions. If you're really considering something like this, well...it needs planning. Backing.
That's why I need you.
I can handle it. I've been waiting for it.
Just give it some thought. Something like that would require a lot of planning, thinking, and backing from the family. Otherwise, everything would fall apart.
That's why I need you.
I can handle it. I've been waiting for it.
No, I...I understand. I only ask that you consider this seriously before you do anything. You'd need to plan it. You'd need the backign of the family - otherwise, it'd all fall apart.
That's why I need you.
I can handle it. I've been waiting for it.
We...we'll talk about this later. For now, I need to deal with the body.
I'll stay here.
I'm coming with you.
Let's...take care of the body first.
I'll stay here.
I'm coming with you.
...Thank you. I'm just...going to grab some tools from the trunk, and then head to the pier. I'll be right back.
Good luck.
...I see. Alright. There's some rope and tools in the trunk - go grab them. No need to drag this out.
[Get to it]
Right. I'll be over soon. I promise.
[Stay by the car]
Clarissa, I...what about tradition? What about...me? All of us?
Join me.
You can do what you want. I'm leaving.
I'll do my best. Seems the only reasonable thing to do. Right now, though...I need to take care of the body.
Alright. I'll stay here.
I'm coming with you.
I hope so. You have my support, if nothing else. Now, let's...I need to take care of the body. Get it over with.
Alright. I'll stay here, if that makes you feel better.
Not alone. I'm coming with you.
...Clarissa, just...
Please, just listen to me. I've been thinking about this a lot, and I might have a plan.
No. Hear me out. You owe it to me.
I can fix this. We can fix this.
...Alright. I'm listening.
I'm going to confront my father about this. Set things straight.
This whole thing, our "family" - it's over. I want to start over, create my own syndicate.
...It's simple, really. Carlo is the source of this rot, and I'm going to kill him.
...And just what do you propose to do? Waltz into your father's office and ask nicely?
Yes, in fact. It's high time someone confronted him.
No. I'm going to leave. Start my own syndicate - do things right.
No, I'm going to waltz into his office and kill the son of a bitch.
Decision 1, huh? Cool.
...He's not exactly known for taking advice, Clarissa. And, frankly, especially not from you.
That's why I need your backing, uncle. I can't do this without you.
Trust me. This time, he'll have no choice.
...Clarissa, you're not thinking straight. You're all worked up - seeing a dead body, it does that to you. Let it go.
I need your help, uncle. I need your backing.
I can't let it go. I won't.
Yes. Come with me. It'll be like back in the day, when our name did mean something.
Yes. Our name means nothing now anyway.
I can't...listen, kid. I've been doing this my whole life. I can't just up and...well, what you're asking me.
Please, uncle. You know all this has to stop. It has to change.
It's going to happen, with or without your help. Better be on the right side of history.
You...give it time. Compose yourself. Don't let your temper get the best of you.
All I ask is that you think about it. You know I'm right - if not now, then with time.
Fuck that. You're with me or against me. That's all it is.
...I'll think about it. I can't, won't promise anything. But I'll think about it. For now, we...I need to take care of that body.
I'm coming with you.
Fine. I'll stay by the car, if that makes you feel better.
...We'll talk about this later, when you've calmed down. Don't forget we're here to do something. Stay by the car. I'll be right back.
No. I'm coming with you.
Fine. If that makes you feel better.
No, you're not. Stay here and cool off. I'll be right back.
You could use my help. You know that.
...Fine.
...Good. Just...take a deep breath. Think about this, properly. It'll be over soon. I promise.
It better.
I know it will. You'll see.
That doesn't matter. You don't need this right now - shit, I don't need this right now - and you have to cool down. End of discussion.
If it's so important to you...fine.
Alright. Enjoy your "touch-up", old man.
...Whatever.
Decision 3, huh? Cool.
...I'll be right back.
[Stay by the car]
Thank you. This will be over soon. I promise.
[Stay by the car]
Decision 2, huh? Cool.
We're here.
Good. Let's not waste any more time.
...This is it? It's worse than I imagined.
It's so...distant. I can't even see the highrises from here.
We have to do a bit of walking. Down the path there, over the dam.
The dam? I thought this was an industrial district.
You know this place well, it seems.
Alright. Lead on.
That's why it's a good spot. No one comes here. Not even homeless junkies. Dam's too loud.
The dam? I thought this was an industrial district.
No one except us, you mean.
Then let's make this quick. You lead the way.
It is what it is. No one comes out here anymore. Not much to see other than abandoned buildings...and the dam, I suppose.
The dam? I thought this was an industrial district.
You mean no one except us.
Then this will be quick. You lead the way.
The dam was here first, the rest followed after. Then again, it's not much of either of those things now. Place is deserted, and the dam is automated.
And yet you're no stranger to this place.
Not much to see, then. Let's get a move on.
...There really is nothing nice out there, Clarissa. Please, stay by the car. I'll be back in no time.
You already agreed. We're doing this together.
...No, you're not leaving me alone out here.
Why?
Doesn't make this whole area any less inhospitable. Listen, Clarissa - stay by the car, won't you? I'll be back in a second.
You already agreed. We're doing this together.
...No, you're not leaving me alone out here.
Why?
It's just routine. It won't be interesting, it won't take long, and it certainly won't be pretty.
It's a body, isn't it?
I don't care about 'pretty'. We're taking care of family business, and this family includes me. End of discussion.
You don't need to protect me from anything, uncle.
...Yes.
I...want to see it.
Well, if it's family business, I should be a part of it.
Lead the way, then.
I assure you, you'll be safe. This will be quick anyway - no need for you to walk all that way for nothing.
"Nothing". I heard what you said earlier. It's a body, isn't it?
I don't care about 'pretty'. We're taking care of family business, and this family includes me. End of discussion.
You don't need to protect me from anything, uncle.
There are more savory parts of the business you could take part of, Clarissa.
I don't want 'savory', uncle. I want the whole picture.
Stop trying to protect me. I can handle myself.
I already came this far. It'd be ridiculous to stay back and wait now.
It's...she's...
Just a girl.
...I think I'm going to be sick.
She's what, uncle? Go on. Tell me.
Never argued you couldn't handle yourself, but this...it's not going to be nice.
We're going. That's that.
I already came this far. It'd be ridiculous to stay back and wait now.
I don't care about 'nice'. I'm not a child, uncle.
This is no place for a...you. It's rough, filthy and unpleasant. The sooner we get back to the city, the better.
You don't need to protect me, uncle.
But it's better if he doesn't. For both of us, Clarissa. That's why I'm asking you to stay here. Let's not take any risks.
What risks, exactly? What are you afraid I'll see?
We'll be careful, uncle. Trust me.
...And he'd be even more furious if you'd come back asking questions. Not just at you, but at me as well. Let's not take that risk.
And what is that risk, exactly? What would I be asking questions about?
Then we'll be careful, and not mention anything to him.
I'm not sure. I'm just unsure about all this, and I have the feeling you shouldn't be here. That it'll change you. Maybe I'm wrong.
There's only one way to find out.
I've no intention on changing. I just want to see clearly.
I'm expecting it to change me. That's why I'm here.
I suppose so. One last time, Clarissa - are you certain you don't want to stay here?
What do you think, uncle?
No. But it's too late to turn back now.
Yes. Now let's go.
Seeing things is one thing - seeing them clearly is another. Are you certain you want to come with me, Clarissa?
You think I'd want to stay by the car, after coming all this way?
No. But I can't turn back now.
Yes. Let's go.
Just don't make any rash decisions, Clarissa. Don't pass judgement too quickly. For my sake.
You know I can't promise that.
I promise. Now lead on.
I don't like it - but I know that look in your eye. Arguing with you now is useless. Just don't...touch anything, alright?
We'll see. What happens, happens.
What look? All I want is to see things clearly.
I will if I have to - and that will be my choice, uncle.
...No. Let's get a move on, then.
Finally.
Lead the way.
...You've never been out this far, have you?
No. I know you have, though.
I'm usually not allowed to.
Only once.
I think I knew that, too. If only it weren't so. Come on, then. Let's get the job done.
Thank you.
Lead on.
Carlo is old-fashioned. You know that. Having a...capable daughter isn't exactly one of his aspirations.
Neither was having a daughter in the first place.
It will be, once he sees what I can do for the family.
...You know how he deals with things, Clarissa.
Leave him to me. I can handle it.
You and me have been through worse. How bad could it be?
I suppose we could. I still don't like it. If he finds out that we lied, well...
Then we'll deal with it. He will, too.
He won't.
He still loves you, Clarissa.
You don't even believe that yourself, do you?
...I'd like to believe that.
...No. But I wish I could. I wish a lot of things were...simpler. Come on. Let's go.
Lead on.
No, no. It's not just enforcement - sometimes things get out of hand. Some things can't be explained away. The touch-up is, well, making sure those mistakes remain unknown. To the public, anyway.
Don't be so vague. Tell me exactly what it is.
So we're here to sweep someone else's mistake under the rug?
So who else knows we're here?
It is what it sounds like. Someone...made a mess, and we're here to clean it up.
You could have just said that at the beginning.
So we're here to clean up someone else's mess.
...Alright. If that's that, then let's not drag things out. Are you ready?
Yes. Let's go.
As ready as I'll ever be.
At least you're not lacking in confidence. Now - there's no way I can convince you to stay back?
No. Let's go.
What do you think, uncle?
Good. Let's be quick about this, then. Don't want to upset him too much.
...Maybe just a little, though. Shall we?
We'll see. Lead on.
...No. Very well, then. Let's get this over with.
[Lead on]
Finally.
That's about right, yes. Of course, some things always change - they get more difficult. Experience counts for a lot nowadays.
You're saying you've got plenty of experience?
So what is it exactly that needs doing?
I've been doing this for decades, Clarissa. Circumstances change, but the work itself remains the same.
You're saying you're good at it?
And what exactly is the "work"?
I...you know what it is, Clarissa. Surely you do. You're a clever girl.
Mhm. And you're good at it?
That's not what I asked, uncle.
Maybe I do - but I'd like to hear it from you, so I don't make any assumptions.
One just wants to be tactful about it. Subtlety is an important part of what we're doing - not just the task itself, but also when talking about it.
Then we'll be subtle - but since I'm helping, I'll need you to fill me in. What do we know about this situation?
Something like that. Yes.
So what do we know about this particular mistake?
...Yes. It's not a pretty job, Clarissa. That's why I wanted you to stay by the car.
Not an option. You know that. Speaking of knowing, what do we know about this particular cleanup?
No. There are others, and...well, possibly. Truth be told, I wasn't told a lot about this one. Usually don't need much of a briefing with my expertise.
Alright - so what DO we know?

Usually, the don. Maybe his advisor, maybe a capo or two - and the ones responsible for the mess. Sometimes a pocket cop will ask for a bribe, other than that, these affairs are taken care of quietly.
And you? What do you know about this one?
No. No, of course not. All I'm saying is that I'd rather not take any additional risks.
What risks, exactly? Me seeing something I shouldn't?
We'll be careful, uncle. I promise.
Not much. Got word from one of the other capos. Told me it was cleared with your father. All I got was the location, and, well, that's usually enough for me.
You're not curious?
"Go to this address and clean our mess" is enough?
That can't be everything. There's something you're not telling me.
Sometimes I am - but usually, the scene is pretty self-explanatory.
What happened, maybe. What about how and why?
That's it? No questions asked?
This other capo - who is he?
Trust me - the fewer questions you ask, the easier it is. Besides, I'm usually the one sending a crew to deal with it. It's rare for me to be personally assigned to a touch-up...I mean cleanup.
Don't you want to know how and why we're here?
Isn't that a good reason to question it?
This other capo - who is he?
Believe me, Clarissa. It's usually better to not know what happened.
...What about how it happened, or why?
That's it? No questions asked?
This other capo - who is he?
There are rules. A hierarchy, a system. Once you've been in the business as long as I have, you learn to trust that process. Trust that people are doing their best.
What if someone isn't doing their best? Doing the opposite, even?
And that's what you're doing?
They're talked to. Set straight. Reprimanded by someone in charge - whatever's deemed necessary.
And if that person is the one in charge?
And who decides that?
Right. I suppose that makes sense.
...Right. Of course. It just works. Great. Sure is a good thing we have these rules.
What are you trying to say, Clarissa?
You're getting played. You must see that.
They know you don't tend to ask questions. What kind of work does that leave you with?
If my father cleared the order, why wouldn't he tell you himself?
I've been doing this a long time. If something was up, I'd see it. Now come on, we've still got some walking to do.
[Keep walking]
...Let's get going, alright? We can talk more on the way.
[Keep walking]
Just think about it. That's all I ask.
I do my job. That really is all there is to it.
I don't think you really believe that.
I guess so.
You're setting yourself up to be taken advantage of.
...Fantastic. What an insightful way to look at things.
You're on thin ice as it is, Clarissa. If your father knew you were here with me...
He won't. I won't tell him, and neither will you.
...He'd be furious. I know. I don't care.
I don't care whether he knows or not.
Another capo. That's all that matters.
You don't think that's a little naive?
What's his name?
Do you trust him?
...What do you mean, Clarissa?
You're getting played. You must see that.
They know you don't tend to ask questions. What kind of work does that leave you with?
If my father cleared the order, why wouldn't he tell you himself?
Isn't it? Come on, Clarissa. We still have lots of walking to do. Let's keep moving.
